title: US Key Themes 2027
gist: Oxford Economics' highest-conviction 2027 call is US GDP growth of 2.5%, well above the 2.1% consensus, driven by a still-running AI buildout and AI-wealth-supported consumers — but with sticky core inflation, noisy divided-government fiscal policy, and debt-financed investment plus a postponed AI labor adjustment sowing a more painful next recession.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics' highest-conviction 2027 call is US GDP growth of 2.5%, up from 2.4% in 2026 and well above the 2.1% consensus.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Positions for upside US growth surprises versus consensus in 2027.
insights.quote: Our highest-conviction call for 2027 is that economic growth will be comfortably above the consensus.

insights.claim: The US economy enters 2027 having absorbed an energy price shock, a hawkish Federal Reserve shift, and a change of control in Congress.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Resilience to stacked shocks underpins the above-consensus call.

insights.claim: US growth resilience masks an economy that is reliant on a single engine: AI.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Concentration risk: US macro is levered to AI capex continuing.
insights.quote: That resilience masks an economy that’s reliant on a single engine.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics says the US AI buildout has more room to run in 2027, while the non-AI economy rebounds and growth broadens across industries.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Broadening growth supports cyclicals beyond AI beneficiaries.
insights.locator: Theme 1: The AI buildout has more room to run

insights.claim: US households' high exposure to AI stocks will support consumer spending through a wealth effect, per Oxford Economics.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Consumer discretionary is now correlated with AI equity performance — an AI sell-off would hit spending.
insights.locator: Theme 1: The AI buildout has more room to run

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects US core inflation to stay above consensus in 2027 because of repeated shocks, bottlenecks and a solid underlying economy.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Lean against consensus disinflation; favors inflation-protected exposure over long nominal duration.

insights.claim: Divided US government in 2027 will bring bruising fights over shutdowns and the debt limit while doing little to curb tariff, immigration and geopolitical uncertainty.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Expect episodic Treasury-bill and volatility dislocations around debt-limit deadlines.
insights.locator: Theme 3: Fiscal policy mostly adds noise

insights.claim: A deficit-financed bipartisan deal could lift US defense and healthcare spending ahead of the 2028 presidential election, adding to growth and inflation.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Upside optionality for defense and healthcare names; upside risk to deficits and yields.
insights.locator: Theme 3: Fiscal policy mostly adds noise

insights.claim: Oxford Economics warns a debt-financed investment surge, weak small-business hiring and a postponed labor-market adjustment to AI are sowing the seeds of a more painful next US recession.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Build hedges for a deeper-than-usual next downturn, especially in credit tied to AI capex.
insights.locator: Theme 4: The seeds of the next recession

insights.claim: When the next US downturn arrives it will have less cushion from fiscal policy, per Oxford Economics, though vulnerabilities are unlikely to cause major problems in 2027.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Near-term benign, medium-term fragile: favors risk-on 2027 with longer-dated downside protection.
insights.locator: Four themes will shape how 2027 unfolds
